Missions_en|223729699057938485: The 34th day of the year 100500 by the Undead reckoning. I began my career in show biz, as the Undead call it. With my first ‘performance’ I need to impress the Sarranga tribe. They will attack and I will kill them. Then I'll turn them to my side.
Missions_en|223729699057938487:
Before you could turn the last dead Sarranga into another zombie, the Twilight one showed up at your chambers. He solemnly announced that you had passed the initiation rite and were ready to become a bearer of the Song.

From now on, he said, your main and only mission would be cultural expansion. The Undead aim to reach it through their music. And mass murder. Starting with Sarranga.

There was a shaky peace between the Undead and the local tribes before your arrival. But if you build a Citadel on disputed territory, it will provoke Sarranga to attack. Thus allowing you to launch a "retaliatory" crushing blow...
Missions_en|445906805903437824:
So, My Lord, you and I are in disputed territory. And I've always thought disputes are a waste of time. The plan is to kill any Sarranga who attack us and declare the territory ours. That's my solution. No one left to argue about anything.

Besides, we have a secret weapon: you, that is. According to Archlich Goya's prophecy, one day a player will appear in Diplomacy is Not an Option who will teach the entire Uncharted Continent, and then the entire virtual world, to listen to the innermost sounds of the Song. I think My Lord is the one Archlich was talking about.

We're at the beginning of our journey, you're not even a musician yet. But you will become one. In the meantime, let's get to some good old-fashioned ultra-violence.
Missions_en|445906805903437825:
My Lord, if you're familiar with the For the King plot branch, you might experience a bit of deja vu soon.

You see, there is one character in the world of Diplomacy is Not an Option who is plotted to lead the attacks in more than just this mission. And I have certain views on this character...

Anyway, the attacking wave's coming, so you're about to understand what I mean for yourself.
Missions_en|445906805903437826:
Look how energized she is. To send so many Sarranga at us at once... Well, let's just remember her young and beautiful. And enraged.

As for her troops, they don't need to be remembered. Instead, we'll make some zombies out of them.
Missions_en|445906805903437827:
My Lord, my calculations were correct! Shankhar has gone totally and irrevocably mad. Every one of her warriors capable of holding a weapon is coming to attack us. This means that when we win, there will be no one to protect our poor Princess of Sarranga. Uh-oh. How did it come to this, I wonder?

Anyway, this is the final attack. As usual, all the Sarranga on the map that you haven't killed will join in. Silly bastards. They could have escaped. Except the program code won't let them.
Missions_en|441585140088422400: Kill all the Sarranga in the area, otherwise they will join the final attack
Missions_en|365078616860372994:
Surprisingly, the undead actually vanished into thin air as soon as the last stone marked the completion of the Temple of Joy.

Along with Shankhar and Snoot, you immediately headed to the chiefs of the Sarranga Tribes' Union to tell them the news of the "Large victory", as Princess called it.

Along the way, you encountered not a single ghoul, not even the mangy one. Nevertheless, once you reached Niniende safely, you tried not to get your hopes up. After all, life convinced you that your luck is made of glass, if not clay, and it tends to shatter...
Missions_en|186833502343114787: December ?20? 1491. It's all gone. The king declared a manhunt for me. The Sarranga have banished me from their lands. In desperation, we fled to the mountains that Shankhar called sacred. It soon became clear that here are the hunting grounds of highly unpleasant giant beetles. If we want to reach the sea in one piece, we must get rid of the damn locusts.
Missions_en|186833502343114789:
Stepping onto the Holy Freaking Grounds will lock The "Simple" Way mission.

Exiled from the lands of Sarranga without a clear answer why, you were making your way to the sea. You never found any treasure, and even the looted basalt had to be returned. Well, thank goodness they didn't take the area map.

Your faithful servant Snoot and equally faithful battlemate Shankhar offered you a choice of two paths.

As a man who was fed up with the protracted expedition, you decided to take the most obvious and the shortest route. Thus you headed to the Sacred Mountains...
Missions_en|304286692872663040:
My Lord, we are in the Sacred mountains of Sarranga. As it often turns out, this time we're not alone.

The point is, these lands are infested with predatory insects. It is not about bedbugs, mosquitoes, and gnats, but about creatures of impressive size and remarkable numbers.

The main problem with insects is that they breed incredibly quickly. If we don't solve that problem at once, I'm afraid we'll be eaten. So, My Lord, I think it's absolutely necessary to kill every last one of those damned bugs and don't forget to destroy their nests.
Missions_en|304286692897828864:
My Lord, we received a message from one of the Chiefs on the Sarranga Council. I am deeply regretful to admit that I have not learned a word of their language during our wanderings, so the meaning of the message remains a mystery. However, the tone chosen, which can be judged by the inherent sentimentality of Sarranga's writing, is quite troubling.

I gave this letter to Princess Shankhar. Her progress in learning our language is amazing. I daresay she will be able to translate it, and we will see if my worries are justified.
Missions_en|304286692897828865:
My Lord, Princess Shankhar translated a message from the Chief. Among other things, the Chief expressed concerns about our doings during the stay in Sacred Mountains. He was quite explicit that if we harmed the giant mole crickets, he would personally come to retaliate against us.

He also asked for a response assuring him that we had no intentions to antagonize nature. He even gave us a deadline. A reasonable one, I must say. Until then, he would have waited for our letter humbly. Without preparing for war.

But the translation took too long. And if I am correct, the Chief is already raising an army to restore order in Sacred Mountains.
Missions_en|304286692897828866:
My Lord, a new message from the Chief has arrived. It was quite short, so Princess translated it for you in less than an hour.

Unfortunately, my worst fears are confirmed. Our temperamental correspondent didn't have the patience to wait for your reply. The chief is already assembling an army and will be here soon.

If I were you, I would dispose of any evidence that might tie us to the decreased population of giant Coleoptera.
Missions_en|304286692897828867:
My Lord, our vigilant scouts report the Chief's army is only a week away. I wouldn't worry too much, for we have, metaphorically speaking, stirred up a colossal anthill.

I doubt the Chief will make it to our position without casualties, for the angry Killer Phasmid will hardly consider him an ally.
Missions_en|304286692897828868:
My Lord, I must inform you that there is an error in my assessment of the strategic balance of forces. It's due to I had no reason to believe the Chief could communicate with man-eating beetles.

To put it simply, our stronghold is about to be attacked by an army of Sarranga, reinforced by the Coleoptera species with amazing wingspans.
Missions_en|304286692897828869:
My Lord, there's a mail hawk from one of our observant scouts. He - I mean the scout, not the hawk - discovered an incredible passion for the study of entomology.

The scout claims that all the local insects are actually of the same species. Some of them spew acid, some have very thick shells. They also have Queens, which are the most threatening. Amazing, isn't it?

As troublesome as it may be, I suggest destroying as many nests of giant beetles of all sorts as possible, because that way we can reduce their population, which will make our lives much easier.
Missions_en|304286692897828870: Destroy all the bugs in the area or they will join the final attack
Missions_en|223729699053744160: December ?20? 1491. I'm going to extreme measures for the sake of the Resistance. If I must be eaten alive by Giant Insects to win Sarranga's support, so be it. Except, I won't be eaten. It's the Insects who will be exterminated in the name of the freedom of Samreignians.
Missions_en|223729699053744162:
Going through Beetle Pass will lock the Heffalump Country mission.

After evaluating the difficulty of both of the challenges, you decided that the "Living among the Beetles" task is not even a challenge.

Bugs and ants, mosquitoes and gnats, biting and buzzing things of all colors are constantly hanging around those who spend a lot of time on the road. Not to say that this neighborhood is a pleasant one, but after all, what can some insects do to the Resistance?

Having reasoned so, you bravely led your men to Beetle Pass...
Missions_en|388480100599705600:
Meelord, you must be careful.

Some Sarranga know how live with bugs. But I am not that Sarranga. And you're not Sarranga at all.

If bugs find us, we be in big trouble. I think we should kill them all. Before they find us.
Missions_en|388480100725534720:
My lord, we've received the first reports from our watchful scouts.

Firstly, the insect attacks are not haphazard. We appear to be dealing with some sort of swarm consciousness. And right now, this evil mind, alien to our understanding, is assessing who it's dealing with. I would compare it to a combat reconnaissance.

Secondly, our settlement is surrounded by impassable mountains to the West and East. Therefore, we should not expect a massive attack from those directions.

I think this also defines the direction of our possible counter-offensive against these wingless biters.
Missions_en|388480100725534721:
Meelord! Your pop-eyed scout send a bird. He tied paper to bird. On paper are words. And, as your counselor calls it, "lustration." Though I think it's a picture.

Bugs are in picture. A swarm of bugs. Very-very nasty. I'm sorry, but I can't do this. Don't tell anyone, but when I see bugs, my hair moves.

I rather hide and wait for you to shred whole swarm.
Missions_en|388480100725534722:
My Lord, our vigilant scouts continue to gather details of the killer cockroaches' maneuvers. They've found certain vulnerabilities in their tactics.

We learned that destroying bug nests reduces enemy activity. As for the quantity of the nests in the surrounding lands, our scouts report - quoting - "They are #%$*ing everywhere" - end of the quote.

I would recommend finding and eradicating these nests to minimize the damage that the incessantly breeding man-eating grasshoppers can cause.
Missions_en|388480100725534723:
Meelord, I am embarrassed, so I come back to you. You killed bugs already, right?

Aaah! Here they come again! Why they still alive? "'The Resistance' is no good!" How do you fight your ex-Chief? You can't even fix bugs!

Sorry, go to cellar again. Lock meself from the inside.
Missions_en|388480100725534724:
My Lord, the evil swarm mind I spoke of earlier seems to have chosen a tactic that the Gorgoth Empire calls by the catchy phrase "Tserg Roush". Which approximately translates to "We spare none of our own."

Its essence is to take a couple thousand of the most lightly equipped and untrained combat units and use them all at once.

The analog of such units among the local bloodsucking сentipedes are those who we classified as "Runner" bugs.

Everything indicates that once they hatch, they run to attack the last outpost of the Resistance.
Missions_en|388480100725534725:
My Lord, we did discover the tactics of the enemy's inflamed and insidious swarm consciousness. Naturally, it is applying Gorgothian Tserg Roush.

However, I was overconfident in my estimation. It appears that the attacks we've seen before were, if I may say so, just a calibration of the "Runner" bugs targeting system.

The last outpost of the Resistance will experience the real Gorgothian "Tserg Roush" by the local Coleoptera version very soon.
Missions_en|388480100725534726: Destroy all the bugs in the area or they will join the final attack
Missions_en|223729699053744165: December ?25? 1491. If it takes a hunting trip to win the Sarranga's support, every Resistance soldier becomes a hunter. But when taking trophies, each member of the Resistance must remember that they are doing so for the citizens of Samreignia. For people who suffer under the tyrant's oppression.
Missions_en|223729699057938432:
If you head to Heffalump Country, you won't be able to see the beauties of the Beetle Pass mission, because it will become inaccessible.

After thinking hard about the challenges the Sarranga Chiefs had given you, you immediately realized which one was easier to complete.

From childhood, you were trained to hunt. On rabbits and foxes, on wolves and boars. You've even killed a crocodile once (though it lived in the moat of your family castle). Anyway, getting trophies, including the tusks of Heffalumps, is a simple matter for an experienced trapper.

Beasts remain beasts everywhere, even on mysterious continents. So, without further ado, the Resistance went on a big hunt...
Missions_en|388731769442906117: Kill all the Heffalumps in the area or they will join the final attack
Missions_en|388731769405157376:
Meelord, I confess. Never saw Heffalump with my eyes. I only hear tales as a child.

In tales Heffalump never stops. He run-run forward and trample everybody in his path.

If someone kill Heffalump, its family take revenge. And Heffalumps are all a big family. So, all for one. And one for all. You to kill a lot of them.

Good thing, there are many tusks to show Sarranga after!
Missions_en|388731769442906112:
My Lord, I am not that advanced in the natural sciences. However, even my knowledge is enough to conclude that we are dealing with a migration. Apparently, the so-called Heffalumps are moving to greener pastures, heading from north to south.

It's worth adding that they are grouped in herds, and their migration route lies through the gorge where the last outpost of the Resistance (I mean the Townhall) is located. And since we're surrounded by high cliffs to the West and East, sooner or later all the Heffalumps in the area will run through our territory, which I think is fair to qualify as a disaster.

I would advise artificially reducing the population of these uniquely clumsy and thick-skinned creatures. After all, by hunting them one by one or in small groups, we reduce the numbers of migrating herds in the long term.
Missions_en|388731769442906113:
Meelord, your eyesie scout sent bird. On bird is piece of paper. I unfold paper and there are words and a picture.

I don't understand words. And picture don't understand too. One thing I understand: It is a sandstorm or Heffalump stampede. If Heffalumps stampede, you can't count them. Because of dust clouds under their feet.

But without dust, you can't count them too. By the time you end count, you are trampled down.
Missions_en|388731769442906114:
My Lord, my worst fears about the population of migrating Heffalumps have proved frighteningly accurate.

If the pause between herds gave you cause for optimism, I have to disappoint you.

Apparently, these giant, tireless creatures are highly intelligent. All Heffalumps are herded together, which increases their chances of avenging their untimely departed kin.
Missions_en|388731769442906115:
Meelord, your cheerful scout send another bird. I took the paper off bird. No drawing this time. I try to read, very long. And I read!

That's because the letters are very big. But I'm so good!

The paper say: THEY ARE COMING!
Missions_en|388731769442906116: My Lord, may I introduce you to the last migrating herd of Heffalumps?
Missions_en|223729699057938465:
?November 29th? We succeeded in evacuating the people of besieged Niniende. The Sarranga followed us because we gave them hope. A chance to survive. We hid at the foot of the Smoky Mountains. Now we are to build a city, expecting all the Sarranga who fled the war to come to us. Our enemies are unlikely to make it into the mountains. It's cold here, and food is a rare find. But will we survive this harsh winter ourselves?

Resource extraction speed is reduced.
Missions_en|223729699057938467:
The same way mindless songbirds can't see the difference between a trapper's handicraft and their kin, people can't tell their dreams from obsessional thoughts. But birds have a good life afterwards. They may just sit in a cage in the living room of some pompous collector of blue blood and tweet. Dreams, however, are more complicated.

Take you and Shankhar. First you build cities, then you drag yourselves across the country with the head of a dead monster. What for? To crawl into the cold, snowy mountains with the few who lived through the siege of Niniende.

The idea of restoration of the great Sarranga Empire was shattered by the question of survival. You and Shankhar had to say goodbye to your dreams and face this new, unfriendly reality...
Missions_en|415544930716200960:
Meelord, we're in Smoky Mountains. It is freezing cold here. You say a good master don't walk his dog when weather is like this.

Sarranga don't have no dogs. Only bombuses. But we have wargs in Smoky Mountains. If I understand good, wargs are like dogs. But big and very wild. Can't tame them. But they have warm skins. When Blizzard, Sarranga wrap in wargs skins to be warm.

One warg just outside your Townhall. You skin him. Because storm can howl.
Missions_en|415544930783309824:
My Lord, our dedicated scouts, who fear no snow, hail, cold, or wargs, have explored the area.

I'd like to say that so far, our idea of moving people out of the war zone is working. Our city seems to be a more attractive place for Sarranga, despite the harsh climate. We just have to wait for all the refugees from Niniende to get here, and Sarranga will have enough men to fight back.

However, My Lord, the conditions in the Smoky Mountains are indeed harsh. We will not have an easy winter. According to our scouts, there is a mountain and a forest northwest of here. I would recommend searching for resources in that direction.
Missions_en|415544930783309825:
My lord, a Blizzard is coming. The people won't survive it without warg cloaks, as Milady rightly pointed out.

If there aren't enough hides, scientifically speaking, the city's population will begin to dwindle.

I would also like you to note that the cloaks Sarranga make are not particularly wearable. When the weather improves, we'll have to stock up on new warg hides. To make new cloaks to survive the next Blizzard.

One last thing. With the temperature drop that's coming, I doubt we'll be able to keep our resource extraction at the same level. I think we should prepare for the worst, My Lord. People will begin to freeze and die, causing the economy to slow down considerably.
Missions_en|415544930783309826:
Meelo... -Cough- ...ord... I give my cloak to little baby girl, newborn. Good that Blizzard end soon. It be warm.

-Cough- But wargs. Danger. When the Blizzard over. They come out of their caves. They hunt.

Be careful. -Cough-.-Cough-,-Cough-, Meelord.
Missions_en|415544930783309827:
Ahchoo!

Meelord. I fear it to be so... -Cough- Wargs — clever beasts. They talk to each other. Call to each other. -Cough-

So less food in Smoky Mountains. And when Blizzard, everyone starve. Wargs are always hungry. Always. Ahchoo!

They know they can eat you, me, Sarranga. They to attack us. From everywhere. Run to -Cough-, -Cough-, -Cough-... Smoky Mountains. To hunt people.

And now, -Cough-, -Cough-, -Cough-. Never stop. Now always attack when Blizzard. When they really angry. Ahchoo!
Missions_en|223729699057938490: The 88th day of the year 100500 by the Undead reckoning. Time for the first big gig! They say the Sarranga capital, the city of Niniende, is full of miserable mortals. They're all just dying to become our fans!
Missions_en|223729699057938492:
Mastering the performing arts is hard work in itself, and if you're chosen to spread the Song of the Undead, it can be a pain in the backside. Especially when sitting behind a drum kit.

But when you're dead, it's easier to become a living music legend. You don't waste time on sleep, meals, and other useless little things. So you can give your best to the Song.

On the road to Niniende, Lords in Black started to sound really good. As befits a band leader, you decided to do an open rehearsal for your ‘fans’ before the first big show. And before truly mass slaughter...
Missions_en|445906805903437828:
My Lord, we are at the approaches to Niniende. Time to enlighten every last Sarranga to the sacred meaning of the Song. Of course, they will resist. And of course, they'll fail.

Well, since you have become a true Death rockstar, the devs and I decided to turn this mission into a real drive. Usually, when you attack enemy cities in Diplomacy is Not an Option, your goal is to destroy some specific buildings, because normally when you attack a city, you want to capture it...

But you and I are not conquerors, we are pilgrims spreading the true faith of the Song. So we have no need for heretical cultural heritage here, and we will raze all the Sarranga buildings to the ground!

Muah-haa-haa-haaaa!
Missions_en|445906805903437829:
Okay, My Lord, our strategy is clear: wipe out the Sarranga. As for the tactics, perhaps I should provide some clarification.

I'm here to play the role of your "vigilant scouts". Which you don't have when you play for the Undead. To be honest, they don't exist in other plot branches either: these scouts are a figment of the writer's imagination.

We are attacking Niniende from the North (which means we may be counterattacked from the South). The capital of Sarranga is located in a canyon that protects it (and us too) from the West and East.

Whatever to do with all this intel is up to you. You are the Chosen One here, after all.
Missions_en|445906805903437830:
My Lord, remember me saying we should destroy all the Sarranga buildings? Well, you might want to get rid of some of them more quickly. Cause from now on Sarranga tents spawn troops that may become a nuisance to us.

It's not a big deal, actually. After all, we'll always find how to use more zombies. But to save us some time dealing with Niniende, it'd be better to destroy Sarranga tents ASAP.

Some of them are located inside Niniende, protected by city walls. There's no easy way to get to them. But there are a couple more outside the wall. Those are the ones I recommend you to start with.
Missions_en|445906805903437831:
Ahem, My Lord, as your most vigilant scout, I must inform you that there is a very good chance we're going to get our asses kicked.

You didn't think an attacking mission wouldn't involve enemy attacking waves, did you? It's core gameplay mechanics, after all. And the game's "USP". So the devs put it in almost every mission.

To summarise the points above, prepare your defenses. And save the game.
Missions_en|445906805903437832:
My Lord! I've just received a message from the writer. He says we need some narrative justification that from now they may attack us from the North as well. Blah-blah-blah Sarranga called for help, blah-blah-blah reinforcements are coming. Damn, so trivial!

I'll put it simply: now they will attack us from the North by the mission's game design.
Missions_en|445906805903437833:
Listen, My Lord. I have some not-so-pleasant news for you. The attack you've just repelled will repeat itself. Again and again, at regular intervals.

This could certainly jeopardize our plans. So I suggest you wipe Niniende off the face of the earth as quickly as possible. Before bloody Sarranga tear down our Citadel.
Missions_en|445906805903437834:
Listen, My Lord. I have some not-so-pleasant news for you. The attack you've just repelled will repeat itself. Again and again, at regular intervals. Moreover, your enemies' health will periodically increase. As if you were playing Endless Mode with the ‘’Skilled Survivor‘’ option enabled.

This could certainly jeopardize our plans. So I suggest you wipe Niniende off the face of the earth as quickly as possible. Before bloody Sarranga tear down our Citadel.
Missions_en|186833502343114792: ?December 25? 1491. My expedition is coming to an end. I have failed to find any gold or make friends with the locals. All my efforts have been in vain. The king is against me, the Sarranga is against me. Even the Undead are against me. And now I have another thing to worry about. Huge beasts the size of the tower of Penderain Townhall block the path to the sea. I need to find a way through. But you can't beat nature itself, can you?
Missions_en|186833502343114794:
Taking the "Simple" way will make the Holy Freakin' Grounds mission unplayable.

Exiled from the lands of Sarranga by the tribal council, you decided not to tempt fate and to flee to the seashore.

When it came to the question of route, you did not hesitate to follow Shankhar's advice. Yes, you had to take a detour, yet you hoped to reach the destination without any adventures.

And your hopes were justified: you quickly crossed the sleepy forest, beyond which the fertile plain stretched. Not believing that luck would smile on you for a long time, you ordered to camp and take a break. Life taught you to be prepared for new trials and hardships that have never missed a chance to appear during your journey.
Missions_en|304286692897828877: Kill all the Heffalumps in the area or they will join the final attack
Missions_en|304286692897828871:
Lovely beasties scratch backs on our Townhall! Sarranga believe, beast fear man more than man fear the beast.

Sarranga say to beast: "I will not touch you, and you will not touch me. I go my way, and you go your way."

Usually works. Let's try it. Maybe beasts go away.
Missions_en|304286692897828872:
Meelord, I now understand why no one comes here. Sarranga has a legend. A terrifying one. About Heffalumps. No one believes it. Neither did I.

Well, it's not a legend. Turns out it's true. Those little animals that scratch their backs on Townhall look like Heffalumps. And if they are, it's bad. Heffalumps never forget anything. Never forgive anything.

They take revenge on us now. They come in a herd and trample us dead. Better kill them first.
Missions_en|304286692897828873:
Meelord, you're out of luck. Very, very bad. Not-Alives must cursed you one last big curse. They cripple your luck. Or bend your destiny.

Otherwise, I don't know how we stuck here with scary beasts. The beasts are there, but no trees and rocks. That's too bad.
Missions_en|304286692897828874: Careful. There are Heffalumps everywhere. One of them notice warrior - it run-run after warrior. Boom! Warrior is a wet spot. Heffalump then stop run. But if Heffalump die, he stop run too. Hmmm...
Missions_en|304286692897828875:
Meelord, your counselor got a paper from scouts. He reads it and turns pale. Then run to the bathroom. Then come back, read it again, turn green and run to the bathroom again. He tell me to tell you this: They're coming.

I think Heffalumps are rabid and attack us in herds.
Missions_en|304286692897828876:
Meelord, your counselor escape to the cellar. I'd escape to the cellar too, but your counselor lock it from inside and don't open anymore. Heffalumps are here.

If we survive, it means Not-Alives don't manage to curse you good. Or I bring us here for nothing.
Missions_en|186833502343114797: January 19, 1492. We have succeeded in reaching the seashore. All that remains is to build our ships and return home. The king's expeditionary force will try to keep us out. But I'll be damned if I can be stopped by some expeditionary corps.
Missions_en|186833502343114799:
You made your way to the sea, and looking at the waves, you clearly realized that the root of your troubles, that broken horseshoe on the steed of your fortune, that bug devouring the four-leaf clover of your luck, was the King of Samreignia.

The proof of this was the royal expeditionary corps sent after you. Not only they had orders to capture you. It'd be too chilling. The real problem was they encamped on the same shore from which you intended to sail back.

Holding back from turning green with anger, you gathered a council to discuss a plan that would allow you to get rid of the reigning autocrat once and for all ...
Missions_en|304286692897828878:
My Lord, I am happy to share my joy that we are about to end the chapter of our entertaining, but to my taste, unnecessarily risky adventures in these lands.

We reached the shore of the Halimatyan Sea. I think building ships and setting sails would be a wiser move than sitting here and waiting for new adventures to come after us.
Missions_en|304286692897828879:
My Lord, our scouts, whom I sent for the sole purpose of finding timber suitable for shipbuilding, approached their task with unusual enthusiasm.

They were exceptionally excited about the opportunity to, pardon my familiarity, "Get the hell out of here." And they studied the area thoroughly.

We now know there's a colony of crustaceans along the shore. Quite typical of the local fauna, the crustaceans are huge and hostile. In addition, Ferdinand II's expeditionary corps holds part of the coastline. As for the forest... It has not been located.
Missions_en|304286692897828880:
My Lord, do you remember driving the Undead from their lands?

Perhaps the timing isn't right, and the location is even less appropriate, but still... Now we know exactly where the cast-out Undead were heading... They came here. So they'll be trying to take control of the coastal area and settle the score with us very soon.
Missions_en|304286692897828881:
My Lord, I am back from inspecting the first launched ship. The results of the inspection are what I personally consider to be "more than satisfactory". Certainly, the local wood is not the best material for shipbuilding. And of course, the lack of resin, which is necessary to prevent water from getting inside the ship, affects the quality of the work done.

However, if you ask me if we will be safer crossing the Halimatyan Sea than we are now, the answer will doubtless be yes.
Missions_en|304286692897828882:
My Lord, our scouts selflessly infiltrated the enemy camp, pretended to be Undead, and obtained valuable information.

It turns out that the Sarranga Tribal Council has turned to decisive action. They sent an entire army to exterminate the Undead and prevent them from taking over the coastal area.

Princess Shankhar claims that the Sarranga warriors, having entered a battle trance, won't waste time trying to figure out who they're fighting. In other words, we have to admit that our fortress, due to its geographical location, has become a legitimate target for Sarranga as well.
Missions_en|304286692897828883:
My Lord, do you remember I told you about the local crustacean colony? Princess Shankhar noticed that neither Sarranga nor the Undead were attempting to take a position in the habitat of these amazing creatures.

If we were able to smoke out or destroy all the overgrowth crabs - you could use this part of the coast as a rear area.
Missions_en|304286692897828884:
My Lord, the sixth ship is ready to depart for Abberlore. I will personally ensure this ship is capable of crossing the Halimatyan Sea. My deepest apologies, for duty, will not allow me to return to your chambers.

If the ship is to pass my careful inspection, it will require someone to supervise the loading operations and speed up the pace of work. I am more enthusiastic than ever, and I feel I am the best suited to be that someone.
Missions_en|304286692897828885:
My lord, our scouts, whose devotion knows no boundaries, detected an approaching army in time. Under the current circumstances, I don't think we care if this army belongs to Sarranga or the Undead.

I recommend putting the soldiers on the defensive lines on full alert (and having them stay there until our ships depart).
Missions_en|304286692897828886:
Congratulations, My Lord. We have succeeded in repelling the Sarranga attack. I regret to report that our misfortunes are far from being over.

After the interrogation, the prisoners, who were still in a trance of battle, spilled their guts.

The point is, My Lord, that the Undead are trying to push Sarranga back to the sea. And Sarranga are doing the same with the Undead. Both sides of the conflict believe they can use our fortress if the other side prevails. To summarize, it doesn't matter if an army is retreating or advancing. It doesn't matter if it's pursuing or fleeing. One way or another, they'll still be trying to take your Townhall.

I'm afraid that until either side admits defeat - and knowing Sarranga and the Undead, that is never going to happen - we will be under attack almost all the time.
Missions_en|304570665964253184:
Given that we don't have people with perfect carpentry skills, we shouldn't be too picky about the appearance of the ships. The only requirement that seems relevant to me is the ability of ships to stay afloat long enough to get us to Abberlore.

In that context, it is an unqualified success that we have already launched three ships.
Missions_en|223729699057938435: January 19, 1492. Princess Shankhar escorted my army to the seashore. All that separates me from the march on Samreignia is the Halimatyan Sea. Today begins the building of the Resistance Fleet. And there is nothing that can stand in our way.
Missions_en|223729699057938434: The new fleet of the Resistance
Missions_en|223729699057938437:
There it is, the triumph! After months of fruitless wandering, you have reached the shore. And now all that separates you from the tyrant who enslaved Samreignia is the Halimatyan Sea. Can you feel your heart beating faster?

All you have to do is build ships and sail back to the shores of Samreignia with the loyal men of the Resistance. And kick the crap out of Ferdinand the Fat.

Luck was smiling on you: you'd found the perfect place to build a shipyard. And there were plenty of trees nearby, too. It is true, as Scott Bloody wrote, "Resistance will always face hardship and endure pain, or it will lose its essence." By heeding his teachings, you did not allow yourself to slack off. A true resister against the system must always be on guard...
Missions_en|223729699057938436: The new fleet of the Resistance
Missions_en|388756919869616128:
My Lord, the day True King Scott I dreamed of has come. We will rebuild the Resistance Fleet!

The only obstacle that stands between us and the distant shores of long-suffering Samreignia is the impressively sized crabs.

By a cruel irony of fate, or perhaps by nature, they prefer to set up their colonies in those parts of the coast that are most suitable for dock construction.
Missions_en|388756919869616129:
My Lord, a new force is in our way! In my heart of hearts, I believe it is manageable.

It seems that after we defeated the Undead and... and, shall we say, defeated Sarranga... It's the nature itself that challenges the Resistance.

The giant crabs have launched a vigorous attack. We are fortunate that their pack was born to crawl, but not to fly.

In this context, it is a faint hope that the giant shrimps won't be able to attack from the sea. However, nothing is ever certain.
Missions_en|388756919869616130:
My Lord, word from our keen scouts.

Until now, we have dealt with a relatively small enemy force, by which I mean a numerical superiority of only two or three times. Also usually we've been searching for the source of our troubles and found it many times. But today, the picture is different. Lobsters are coming here from faraway lands, and there is no way to locate the nests that spawn their main forces.

In other words, no matter how many enemy bases, or should I say lobster lairs, we destroy in the vicinity, the attacks will not cease.
Missions_en|388756919869616131:
My Lord, I do not wish to spread alarm and hurt the morale of the Resistance...

However, I am obliged to share the latest intel. It may not be visible now, but the enemy's numbers are steadily increasing. We do not know if this is a targeted attack on the last Resistance outpost, or if it's just that all sorts of obscene-sized crayfish are becoming more active in these lands as winter sets in.

However, if this trend continues, it will become increasingly difficult to survive. Therefore, I advise you, for your sake, for my sake, for the sake of our people, for the cause of the Resistance, to build ships and sail away from this accursed continent.
Missions_en|388756919869616132:
My Lord, the first ship has launched! I personally appointed the captain, and the captain named the vessel. The new flagship of the Resistance is called "Scott the Fearless".

If I may say so, the new flagship looks much more reliable than the one we had at the beginning of our journey.
Missions_en|388756919869616133:
My Lord, the fourth ship is ready to depart for Abberlore. Given the rapidly worsening sanitary situation, namely the invasion of the monstrous Eurypterids, I advise you not to delay the loading of the men.

If we hurry, trust me: our fighters, hardened in the crucible of war with paddlefish of all kinds, will take Abberlore in three days.

Long live the Resistance!
Missions_en|223729699057938470: ?December 20? Princess Shankhar fell seriously ill during our wintering in the Smoky Mountains. Sarranga healers believe she can be cured by an extract from the heart of the Father of Heffalumps. Together with Snoot and a small party, I went in search of this beast.
Missions_en|223729699057938472:
You received only two pleasant memories of the wintering in the highlands of the Smoky Mountains. The first one was about having a deer bone instead of frozen frog stew. And the second one - about traveling down to the valley with Snoot and Shankhar on a wagon. It was the moment you felt that spring was near. Which you realized because your teeth finally stopped rattling.

Though the second memory could hardly be called pleasant. Shankhar, usually strong as a moose, stubborn as a ram, but this time helpless as... as... You couldn't find the right horned animal to complete the metaphor.

Anyway, looking at the powerless and delirious Princess, you could only hurry Snoot who was driving the wagon. Rushing was not exactly a clever move, as you were making your way off-road. And a single wrong driver's movement could overturn the wagon. In the end you've reached the Heffalump Valley...
Missions_en|368323633020252160:
So, you've finally made it here, My Lord! Well, congratulations! Make yourself comfortable.

You probably thought you'd be chasing the boss, occasionally fighting off Heffalumps. Well, I'm sorry to disappoint you: it's not going to be your way. I convinced the devs that the story campaign for Sarranga lacked drama. And that I didn't have enough "screen time". Together, we've found a solution! Though it's more of a problem for you.

Here is the thing: I've defiled the Father of Heffalumps. He's not exactly alive now. At the same time he's not completely dead. I wonder if his heart still has the healing powers to cure your lovely Princess. Well, I guess it's for you to find out.

You can track the movements of my "Frankenstein" on the mini-map. Just for the record, you don't have to hunt him down. Sooner or later, the Defiled Father of Heffalumps will come to your Townhall. The clock is ticking. Will you have time to prepare the welcome party?
Missions_en|368323633020252161:
Behold, my crowning achievement in the necromantic arts! Admit it, it's pretty impressive. Its skin is harder than a pea, and it breeds Undeads in unspeakable numbers.

Oh, forgot to warn you. If you're hoping to kill him and win the mission immediately, you're in for a nasty surprise.

You see, normal, alive Heffalumps think their Father is doing fine. If anything happens to him, they'll come running for revenge. As for me, I'll send in a few more baddies to help finish the job.

That's how sneaky I am today. Because you shouldn't have killed good old Ozzy! An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth!
Missions_en|415921081141800960:
So, I been thinking... How about I tickle your nerves a little?

Luckily for us, there are Undead lairs scattered all over the map. A reminder: lairs normally spawn enemies in this game. So, my undeads will be paying you visits from time to time. You know, to check on your health. And your defenses.
Missions_en|415921081166966784:
$%@$! Do you have any idea how much mana I spent to create this cadaver?! You think you've never met a Nightmare General around here for nothing?

I hope you're satisfied. I hate to admit it, but my Heffalumps's heart was an "original part". So you will save your precious princess after all.

...assuming, of course, you survive the final attack. Ha-ha-haaaaah!
Missions_en|415921081166966785:
My Lord, we are extremely fortunate that you were warned of the consequences of killing the Defiled Heffalump and had time to prepare.

Since that is the case, I feel it is my duty not to distract you from arranging the defense of the settlement. I think it'd be better for me to retire to the cellar.

Call me when the battle is over, and I will bring you some wine to properly celebrate our victory.
Missions_en|415921081166966786:
Have you seen the Jaws movie, My Lord?

If you haven't, that's fine. I'll recreate a couple of scenes for you. My Heffalump will portray the shark. And your Townhall will be sinking "Orca."

Now, the shark — I mean, the Heffalump — is circling around you, getting closer and closer. Very soon, it will attack. And I don't think you can handle a big, bloodthirsty monster, buddy. All that is left for you is to wait for death.

Muah-ha-ha-haaaaah!
Missions_en|358750154038030336: Survive the Heffalump counter-offensive after killing Defiled Father of Heffalumps
Missions_en|368323632974114816: Exterminate all enemies in the area or they will join the final attack
Missions_en|223729699057938495: The 144th day of the year 100500 by the Undead reckoning. Oh, yeah! We're going on a world tour! We need a ship, though. As it'll take us very long to cross the Halimatyan Sea on foot.
Missions_en|223729699057938497:
After the sensational success in Niniende, Lords in Black are set to head to Samreignia. The Twilight One, as the tour manager, apologized for the idiots who invented your fictional world. He complained that "the devs" could have brought some airplanes to the realm.

You actually weren't that upset, since you had no idea how a levitating plain could help. Still, the Halimatyan Sea had to be crossed somehow. By water, obviously.

The Undead wouldn't be themselves if a certain number of living beings didn't have to die during ship construction...
Missions_en|445906805903437835:
Well, My Lord, here they are, the shores of the Halimatyan Sea. As I said, Lords in Black are ready to embark on a transcontinental tour.

Two things separate us from success. One, we don't have a ship. But we do have a defiled shore on which we need to build a shipyard. For that, we must thank Archlich Korador, who three hours before you, My Lord, started the game, fancied himself the Chosen One, and set out to bring the Song to Samreignia. He's never been heard from since. And now we know why.

Which brings us to our second problem. Crabs. Apparently, they've liked the taste of Korador. Which means they wouldn't mind another bite of the undead. We could make them into undead crabs, but trust me, the smell would be unbearable. So we'll just make regular zombies out of defeated crabs somehow.
Missions_en|445906805903437836:
So, My Lord, you've built the Shipyard. Not bad. Now make sure they don't damage it.

The game designer asked me to warn you: when Crabs attack, they certainly won't miss the Shipyard.

We don't want all those spent Bones to go to waste, do we? From now on, My Lord, you've got to defend both: the Citadel and the Shipyard.
Missions_en|445906805903437837:
The moment we leave this continent is getting closer, My Lord!

You're halfway to success. If you and I were in a Match-3 game, you'd be getting some currency right now, some spectacular special effects to keep you involved.

But we're in the hardcore strategy game about survival and construction. So, My Lord, survive and construct.
Missions_en|445906805903437838:
I've left you for one second, and look what you've done! How did you manage to let this happen, My Lord?

I'd understand if it was your first mission. But we've even passed the middle of the walkthrough!

Right, listen, I haven't kept track of the last time you made a save, but maybe you should load an earlier one. It's not like we die farming this enormous amount of Bones to build the new Shipyard, but why waste time on it?
Missions_en|445906805903437839:
Well done, My Lord!

The ship is almost finished. Only one iteration is left to complete the mission.

Have you thought of a name for it yet? How about Suprise, like your grandfather's?

By the way, did you know there's a free version of Diplomacy is Not an Option that just happens to tell the adventure of Duncan Ironbrow?
Missions_en|445906805903437840:
My Lord, I'm broadcasting the traditional "Bad news or the Scouts messed up again" program for you.

You are about to be attacked by crabs once again. That's not a surprise, as you can see it on your mini-map.

What is news, My Lord, is that an Emperor Crab is among the attackers this time. Some kind of a mini-boss, to put it mildly. So far, there's only one. But knowing the devs, I can guarantee you: where is one, there'll be two. Even four before you know it. If not in this attacking wave, but in one of the upcoming ones.
Missions_en|445906805903437841:
You'd better hurry up with that ship, My Lord.

I am saying this for a reason, you know. And this reason is the attack you've just survived is set on repeat.

Furthermore, the crustacean invaders' health will gradually increase. Soon enough, holding them back will become a bigger issue.
Missions_en|460720462445260800:
You'd better hurry up with that ship, My Lord.

I am saying this for a reason, you know. And this reason is the attack you've just survived is set on repeat.
Missions_en|186833502343114802:
A plan developed on the distant shore of an unfriendly continent worked. Which, actually, came as some surprise.

Under the cover of night, you landed in the suburbs of Abberlore with an army ready to follow you to the end and storm the capital of Samreignia.

There was no time to lose. If not capitalized on the effect of the sudden assault, King Ferdinand might be wise enough to call on his loyal feudal lords for help.
Missions_en|186833502343114804: I can tell by the moon that it is March 8th, 1492. The die is cast. King Ferdinand has declared me his enemy, and that is a grave mistake. I have no enemies alive. We returned to Samreignia. We landed just outside Abberlore. Either we take the capital or die. For the first time in my life, everything is certain.
Missions_en|304286692897828890:
My lord, we arrived at the outskirts of Abberlore and even managed to gain a foothold on the coast. However, there have been some changes made to the original planning.

First of all, despite all the precautions taken and the coordinated actions of your troops during the night landing, our arrival did not go unnoticed. Which is regrettable.

Over the past night, as the exhausted but dedicated scouts have informed me, King Ferdinand II prepared the capital for the siege. I fear we have no choice but to storm Abberlore. And unfortunately, without the element of surprise, we were all hoping for.
Missions_en|439458753504194560:
Oh my gods, they killed Marlin!

Your ex Chief have no heart! He pay me for his atrocity.

But for now I return to castle. Need to think how to avenge poor Marlin.
Missions_en|304286692897828891:
My Lord, through stealthy forays behind the walls of Abberlore, we learn that Ferdinand II is preparing to escape. There are several ships in the capital's harbor waiting for the signal. The evacuation is at the stage of loading the most valuable items on board.

Something we can take advantage of. It will be a risky but bold and effective maneuver, allowing us not only to replenish our own gold reserves but also to cut off Ferdinand's only escape route.
Missions_en|304286692897828892:
Meelord, I did a recon mission. I want to tell: your former Chief is a big bag of lies. Hides gold in all forts and posts. Lots of gold.

Why he send you to my land? Why he did that? My people die for nothing. Your people die for nothing. Even Not-Alives... No, these die for purpose. Better world without Not-Alives.
Missions_en|304286692897828893:
Meelord, I an true scout now. I spy on enemies. Your ex-Chief's friends come at us from other side.

First deal with them, then deal with your ex-Chief.
Missions_en|304286692897828894:
You know what you are? An unprincipled jackal! A worthless aphid who's encroached on my ermine mantle. An aspid, whom I warmed on my chest as a baby serpent and fed with milk from my table!

A spineless traitor who cares only for his own filthy bald hide. Surrender now, retreat, and I promise you a quick death. And in my generosity, I'll spare your family. Do you even remember that you have a wife, a daughter, and a son?

You'll never defeat me! I've sent messengers to every corner of my country. Soon my loyal vassals will rid the land of your filthy bearded face.
Missions_en|304286692897828895:
Think for a moment what you're doing, you damned oath-breaker! You're trespassing on the most sacred thing in Samreignia! My authority!

By the way, the country was at peace under my rule. There was poverty, yes. There was famine, but it was you who came here with a sword. It was you who brought the burdens of war upon the long-suffering capital that you, as a knight, were supposed to protect.
Missions_en|304286692897828896:
There are still honest men in my kingdom! Sir Roland Slowpoke and the blacksmith Bryn of Rothglen together established a liberation movement.

They won't rest until they put down your vile rebellion. If you repel one attack, another will follow. You know the Rothglenian stubbornness. As long as there are men in this country who can hold a sword, you can't escape the people's anger.

And if there are no men left, who are you going to rule? Even if you succeed? Ashes? You know your cause is not right! Have courage and lay down your arms!
Missions_en|304286692902023168:
A Trebuchet shell just blew out the Cathedral of the Nine Pilgrims. Bloody vandal, have you any sense of nobility left? This cathedral was the beginning of the city of Abberlore nine centuries ago!

Its roof fell on an orphanage. And I don't have the manpower to clear the rubble.

If you have studied history, you'd know that even during the war for the Independence of Samreignia not one of Inverland bastards' shells fell on Cathedral Square.

You're not just a traitor, not just some rebel. You are pure evil in the very flesh.
Missions_en|304286692902023169:
You continue to amaze me. There are civilians in the city. Women. Children. And you just keep dropping heavy rocks on their heads. Taking away their homes, their lives, killing their hope for a brighter tomorrow.

If you were a true knight, you'd challenge me to a duel. I would, of course, challenge you to Sir Dwayne the Indestructible, commonly known as "The Rock." He'd put you down in a heartbeat. For good. But let's face it, the ordinary citizens of Samreignia would not be bothered by our disagreement.
Missions_en|304286692902023170:
What the hell are you doing, you scoundrel? Why did it have to come to this? We could have arrested you, we could have warned you. A year or two in jail for your misdemeanors. That's all it would take.

You know me, I'm hot-tempered with words, but I'm merciful in my heart. Now, of course, the only mercy I have left for you is to wish you to throw yourself off the castle wall. The armies of my loyal vassals are on their way.
Missions_en|186833502343114805: Storm the Castle of Ferdinand II the Fat
Missions_en|223729699057938440: March 8, 1492. This may be the last entry in my log. Caught by surprise, the King has no time to rally his forces to defend the capital. Yet the enemy still outnumbers us. We are in a position to attack. The die is cast. I believe that today the Resistance will end the tyranny of Ferdinand II once and for all.
Missions_en|223729699057938442:
With an army small but hardened by endless battles on the Uncharted Continent, you have landed at Abberlore.

This is the moment of truth. For the first time in your life, it's simple. It's either you or them. The Resistance will either triumph or its memory will be warped. And your name and the names of all who followed you will be ridiculed and berated, only to end up on the margins of history.

Perhaps when the Resistance dares to attack the capital, the people of Samreignia will throw off the shackles of slavery and rise up after you. Anyway, you've already made up your mind. Abberlore must fall. The banner of the Resistance will fly over the capital!
Missions_en|390898944500936704:
My Lord, news of the Resistance marching to Abberlore is spreading throughout Samreignia!

Unfortunately, as our alert scouts report, the suppressed people have not risen to the occasion and are not ready yet to fight on our side. During our absence, everyone has forgotten about Scott the Bloody and his allies. Besides, few people understand who you are and why you want to storm the capital.

Sadly, after the King had discovered the flag of the Resistance flying dangerously close to Abberlore, he prepared for a siege.
Missions_en|390898944530296832:
My Lord, the Resistance is growing. The unhappy people of Samreignia are awakening and beginning to see the true face of Ferdinand II. Rumor is that the ruler is plotting an escape route from Abberlore.

The capital is full of ships loaded with the King's cargo.

If we requisition the valuables, we'll have more money for the war. And when we are victorious, the surplus can be used to improve the lives of the long-suffering people of our homeland.
Missions_en|390898944530296833:
My Lord, scouts report that Ferdinand's gold is flowing from all over the country to the capital. The cellars of nearby forts and outposts are bursting with unjustly gained wealth.

The Resistance has another opportunity to show that inhumane taxation is the result of the King's inadequate greed, not a necessity. And of course, the Resistance's cause will benefit greatly from this money.
Missions_en|390898944530296834:
Why you a sedition-monger! A heretic! A renegade! You're rotten to the core! Thanks to me, you had everything: lands, vassals, family, even money. All this in times of trouble for our fatherland! And how did you repay me? You've joined up with some village madman, thinking you know better than me what my vassals, entrusted to me by Providence, need.

Who do you think you are? I'm going to sober you up a bit. In no time at all, I raised a militia under my banner. Now, you lousy traitor, the people you claim to protect will attack you from the most unexpected direction.

What will you do? Fighting my guards, the regime's lackeys is one thing. Fighting innocent peasants taking up the sword for the first time is different.
Missions_en|390898944530296835:
My Lord, it seems that not only the idea of the Resistance, but the idea of resistance to the Resistance is gaining ground.

Ferdinand II has set a very generous daily allowance for anyone who enlists in the regular army of Samreignia.

I'm afraid that has clouded the minds of the commoners. Between the dim prospects of a Resistance victory and the obvious benefit of a lightning-fast rise through the military ranks, people are choosing what they usually choose. The immediate prize.

I fear the enemy's attacks will now become as much unpredictable as they are desperate.
Missions_en|390898944530296836:
So why don't you give up and die like a knight? Do you have dignity and honor?

I don't see the people you supposedly represent flocking to your banner in crowds. You alone, no one else wants to shake the boat of my statehood. If you've lived in Samreignia for the last six months, you'd know I had even lowered the land tax.

Mind you, I haven't fallen so low as to blackmail you with the lives of your loved ones. Your son, your daughter, and your wife. Though I could have. But no, they're still in your family castle. And they're safe. Surrender peacefully and I'll leave them alone.
Missions_en|390898944530296837:
Dear ideological rival to the power granted to me by Providence itself, your hand is dealt. Sir Roland Slowpoke and blacksmith Bryn of Rothglen have formed the Samreignian Liberation Army on their own. You see, I don't even pay them! It's about your unity with the people.

Remember the famous Rothglenian stubbornness? Bryn and Roland will not rest as long as you live. If you defeat one attack, another will follow.

So what people and on what terms do you intend to rule? Even if you win?
Missions_en|390898944530296838:
Witness this! The protector of the oppressed people of Samreignia has broken the Cathedral of Nine Pilgrims. It's where the city of Abberlore began over 900 years ago! It was a national symbol. And a tourist attraction.

Thousands of prayers were said there every day to glorify my name. Hell, even the Inverland invaders during the War of Independence never laid a finger on it.

If you win this, know that you are damned for eternity. The people of Samreignia will never forgive you for this.
Missions_en|390898944530296839:
Stop! There are women and children in the city! If you have any compassion for the people of Samreignia, I beg you, stop!

Let us settle this matter man to man. A one-on-one duel according to the code of chivalry. You against Sir Dwayne the Unbreakable, popularly known as The Rock.
Missions_en|390898944530296840:
I realize you're not coming to your senses. You know not what you do or why you do. You are a trial sent by Providence to confirm my right to these lands once and for all.

Only by defeating you, pure evil, will I prove to the people of Samreignia that I am worthy to bear the burden of power. I have no doubt you will be swept away. You must not survive this attack.

Otherwise, I will lose all faith in Providence.
Missions_en|223729699057938443: Storm the Castle of Ferdinand II the Fat
Missions_en|223729699057938475: ?December 31? 1491. King Ferdinand II sent his troops to invade Sarranga lands and enslave the natives. The chiefs have asked for my help. I will take charge of the defence of the last city not taken by Ferdinand. I must drive out the invaders, for the Sarranga are my family now.
Missions_en|223729699057938477:
As a man of honor married to a princess, you must take care of your family. And a prince's family is his people. After brief arguments, even Shankhar agreed that this was not the moment for you two lovers to run away into the sunset.

By revealing the continent's location to the Samreignian government, you've made a mistake. Yet you also had a chance to make it right. To do so, at the request of the chiefs, you have traveled to the city of Chiquinga. The last bastion of Sarranga's independence from Samreignia.

Here, you will give battle to the Royal Army. Those insolent flies on the sweet cake of your family happiness, those sneaky moles who have strayed into the seedbeds of the people's freedom...
Missions_en|414103673129250816:
My Lord, the commander of the King's army expects to crush us with a single blitz attack. I'm afraid we have little time to train our troops and build fortifications. You'll have to improvise and fight with what you have.

Milady Shankhar entered the battlefield. Riding a Heffalump. I understand your desire to keep her safe, but it is she who may create the decisive advantage in the battle.
Missions_en|414103673133445120:
Meelove! Here they come! Now we meet destiny.

Together, until the end! Sarranga will be free!
Missions_en|223729699057938478: Survive the one and only attacking wave
Missions_en|331755100421599232: ?January 14? 1492. I am tired of war. With my beloved wife Shankhar, I have fled to the mountains, where we shall build a new home. Perhaps a peaceful old age in the wilderness is what I have always lacked.
Missions_en|331755100421599234:
When following orders, how often did you take the easiest path, abusing your power and resources to accomplish goals? Have you ever had doubts when your actions could lead to casualties? Have you thought about the lives of others and the ethics of your deeds?

The first time you reflected on it, you kept seeing only new questions. Who are you? A feudal lord? A discoverer? A Sarranga prince? You've never asked for any of these titles.

There's no need for men to die for power, wealth, or ideas they don't share. So you decided to flee with your beloved wife, Shankhar, away from the horrors of war.

Except this time, Snoot refused to go with you. Thus, your paths parted...
Missions_en|331755597652144128:
Meelove! We escape from war. Time to live happily ever after.

But how can we live happily ever after without home? Without children? We must make home and children!

Also we all eat something. I do house and you hunt and gather food.
Missions_en|415113038053355528: Good branches you discover. Dry. Sturdy. I can make a home of them! You gather more branches, I build comfortable house for we.
Missions_en|415113038028189696:
Meelove! Look how big this Deer! He run fast. It means he strong. And It means he have much meat.

You chase he, he hide in caves. Tough hunt. But I believe in you, meelove!
Missions_en|415113038053355520: Meelove, you not much of a hunter. You try and try more, but deer is still healthy. You have to bruise him twice more to get meat. Speed up, meelove!
Missions_en|415113038053355521: Come on, meelove! One more bruise like this and we have nice dinner.
Missions_en|415113038053355522: How good you are, meelove! You are great hunter. Now I see I'm happily married. Finally, steaks and meat broth from yummy Deer!
Missions_en|415113038053355523: Meelove, we have baby! Baby grow up fast and help with house keep. May become berrypicker or fisherman, or may become hunter. In Sarranga, father decide for children where child work. So it's up to you.
Missions_en|415113038053355524:
Meelove, now I make you happy and you jump of joy! I give birth to twins! Much children, much help with work.

I know, with you they become good people. And good workers.
Missions_en|415113038053355525: Meelove! I finished our home! Now it cosy and big, just like I dreamed. And it fit for our big family!
Missions_en|415113038053355526: Meelove! You raise our child a real trapper! You now can hunt better together.
Missions_en|415113038053355527: Ehm... You suggest we eat this, meelove? I could, of course, pickle it. Or, uhm... Dry it. But, meelove, not very tasty. It'll do for a while. But better catch deer.
Missions_en|223729699057938500: The 194th day of the year 100500 by the Undead reckoning. Abberlore, meet Lords in Black! The capital of Samreignia has never seen such a show!
Missions_en|223729699057938502:
It's happening! Your ship has sailed to the shores of Samreignia. The Twilight One congratulated the whole team and mentioned that cool rock bands need a charismatic vocalist. Then he left.

You had no idea who rock bands were or what they needed. But you didn't waste your time, and while Dusky was away, you decided to celebrate your homecoming.

After all, you've had an eternity to conquer Samreignia. Who cares how many times you have to die and ‘re-load?’
Missions_en|445906805903437842:
So, My Lord, we've made our way to the suburbs of Abberlore. In other plot branches, this is the point when your loyal counselor tells you that things didn't go according to plan, the enemy figured out your daring maneuver, and now you have to fight against hordes and storm the capital at the same time (surprise-surprise).

But this time will be different! With Lords in Black, everything always goes according to plan. And everything is under control. The undead don't hide from anyone.

On the contrary, the more enemies attack us (and they will), the more we'll kill! We'll expand our fanbase so impressively that in Diplomacy is Not an Option's sequel we'll get stadiums!

Now, prepare your troops. It's time to conquer the capital!
Missions_en|445906805903437843:
Listen, My Lord, while you and I were dealing with the problems on the Uncharted Continent, the local little king seems to have improved his financial situation. He's got ships full of gold in ports. The outposts are bursting with chests of goodies.

Any undead knows that gold corrupts people. It defiles their souls. In a very wrong way. In fact, the way is so wrong, that these corrupt souls hardly fit for our purposes.

So why don't we take the gold for ourselves and nail it!? Just think of the maneuver: if we take the treasure for ourselves, it will attract more pathetic people trying to steal it from us! That's how many people will rise under our black banner!
Missions_en|445906805903437844:
Listen, My Lord, the devs asked me to ask you if you have the ‘Stock Market Crash’ achievement. If you don't, and you want it badly, I'll give you a hint.

When creating Abberlore, the devs made several buildings specifically for missions where you have to storm the capital. For their hard work not going to waste, they bound a hidden achievement to some of these buildings.

I'm alluding to ports and Abberlore Bazaars. I guess you know what should be done now.
Missions_en|445906805903437845:
I don't know who you are or where you came from, but you definitely came to the wrong town. And to the wrong country. I've personally sent mail hawks to all my feudal lords... Except for one, who's gone missing. He didn't turn out to be a conqueror of uncharted lands.

But I'm not talking about him. It's about my loyal vassals, who shall not tolerate a blatant act of unprovoked aggression against me. Not even feudal lords! No honest Samreignian will forgive your violation of my royal authority. The peasants have already sharpened their pitchforks.

Now you'll be attacked from the most unexpected directions. If I were you, I'd get off my land back where you came from. And I'd pray hardly to Providence that vengeance would not find you in your lifetime.
Missions_en|445906805903437846:
It seems that our Ferdy began to suspect something. Namely, that his situation is desperate. So he decided to raise the daily pay for all the militiamen.

People, of course, took the bait. So the attacks are going to escalate. People obviously are just delaying their final act. I don't know why they're clinging to their pathetic virtual lives. But that's okay, when you complete the mission, they'll all learn the innermost meaning of the Song!

One way or another, you and I, My Lord, will win. Who cares how many times you have to load an earlier save, right?
Missions_en|445906805903437847:
I call upon your mind. Upon the virtues that make us humans. Is there compassion in you? Mercy? Kindness?

I understand the desire to take over someone else's lands. I'm the same, you know. I've been hatching a plan to take Whadford from Inverland for several times.

But what you're doing is a senseless slaughter. Besides men with pitchforks, there are women, old men, children. At least let them leave Abberlore safely. I take it you're not even listening to me...
Missions_en|445906805903437848:
I wish to inform you that news of the invasion of Abberlore has spread throughout the country. Sir Roland Slowpoke and the blacksmith Bryn of Rothglen together established the Samreignian Liberation Army.

You used to fight with scattered groups of volunteer militiamen. Now it's a people's war.

No one has ever conquered a country in which every man stands one for another to the death!
Missions_en|445906805903437849:
Now you crossed every imaginable red line. You've destroyed the Cathedral of the Nine Pilgrims!

Let us assume you're cruel, perhaps some kind of madman. But even a madman wants to rule a city, not ashes!

Think of it! Nine centuries the cathedral has stood. It even survived the battle for the independence of Samreignia. Yet you ruined it so simply. I will pray to Providence that Abberlore will stand. And then, I swear, I will rebuild the cathedral. I will even pay handsomely for its restoration.
Missions_en|445906805903437850:
All the countries I know honor the tradition of Judgement of Providence. It is when two men who sent men to war must face off in a one-on-one duel. The winner is awarded the victory. The loser dies, and then the war is over.

So, I challenge you to the Judgement of Providence. With one little nuance: Ser Dwayne the Indestructible, commonly known as The Rock, will fight for me.

If you refuse, you will be disgraced forever. And there's nothing good waiting for you when you die, either!
Missions_en|462271467536363520:
I realize you're not coming to your senses. You know not what you do or why you do. You are a trial sent by Providence to confirm my right to these lands once and for all.

Only by defeating you, pure evil, will I prove to the people of Samreignia that I am worthy to bear the burden of power. I have no doubt you will be swept away. You must not survive this attack.

Otherwise, I will lose all faith in Providence.
Missions_en|223729699057938503: Storm the Castle of Ferdinand II the Fat
Missions_en|96585428681732096: Stay alive for as long as you can!
Missions_en|96585428681732097:
My lord! The developers know no mercy! They have brought back the endless mode to the demo version.
Now we are doomed to agonizingly die again and again even here!
But look at the bright side: as long as we're alive, we'll be killing mongrels. Terrific, isn't it?
Missions_en|54986981406351361: Stay alive for as long as you can!
Missions_en|54988405670354945: Stay alive for as long as you can!
Missions_en|54977231985778688:
My Lord, this time we don't have a chance.
But let us be positive:
The longer we stand, the more mongrels we can kill.
Missions_en|669183009604231168: Prince Connor isn’t really into keeping a diary, so I, his humble advisor Snoot, will have to take notes. Our first diplomatic attempt was a total flop. Instead of engaging in negotiations, the Gorgothians engaged us in battle (for no obvious reason). Prince decided we should return the favor by destroying the outpost that fired on our ship.
Missions_en|669183009604231169:
A new threat looms over our long-suffering Samreignia: the war with two neighboring powers. His Majesty King Ironbrow, defender of peace, bastion of goodness, and all that, has attempted to resolve the crisis through diplomatic means.

For this purpose, he sent his only son and me, his most loyal servant and advisor, to negotiate with the Gorgoth Empire, which has already managed to seize some of our islands.

Prince Connor is young and inexperienced, but I still have faith that prudence will prevail over the thirst for revenge and that peace will be restored...
Missions_en|669183009604231171:
My Prince!

You have become supreme commander, and I will return to my role of military advisor. Since you are inexperienced in this field, no offense meant, I will place special emphasis on important information for you.

Our situation is rather uncertain. The Gorgothians who attacked us have taken up positions in the outpost and are unlikely to leave it willingly. Therefore, we are forced to strike. What's more, we'll have to lay siege to the fortress with the forces we currently have. The reinforcements won’t be coming from anywhere.
Missions_en|669183009604231172:
My Prince!

We just need to destroy the Gorgothian Magistrate to win. It used to be our Magistrate, but since the Gorgothians have captured, and since their nobility commands their troops from there, it will be easier to simply raze it to the ground...

I remind you that you have a limited military contingent at your command. Which is why, My Prince, I recommend concentrating our attack on single flank. That way, you’ll spare our troops, since the enemy ranged units on the opposite flank won’t be able to shoot them.
Missions_en|703176914641084416: Destroy the Magistrate of Fykee Island
Missions_en|669183009604231176: A Gorgothian assault force has landed on the island housing our border garrison. We are set to face their attack today. Although “today” is a figure of speech in this case, since it’s unclear exactly when the Gorgothians will launch their assault. As I’m writing this, Prince continues to reinforce our fortress’s defense.
Missions_en|669183009604231175:
The consequences of the failed negotiations were not long in coming: The Gorgothian fleet is approaching the Samreignian border garrison. It's not hard to guess why.

Prince and I rushed to help the brave defenders of our homeland. We arrived just in time to discover that they were planning a tactical retreat. Our arrival, however, inspired them to fight on.

Prince Connor is confident that we can defeat the Emperor on the battlefield. One question troubles me: why is the enemy attacking only now, if the so-called “peace negotiations” were a trap from the very beginning?
Missions_en|669183009604231178:
My Prince!

The Gorgothian forces have landed on the shore, but we have time to prepare them a proper meeting. Although it’s commonly believed that the best defense is a good offense, I still advise you get ready for the siege.

This time, you have veterans of the Battle of Fykee Island as well as an entire garrison of Samreignian border guards. More importantly, you can now recruit new soldiers.

With a bit of luck and a well-planned troop deployment, you can certainly fight off the Gorgotians’ attack.
Missions_en|669183009604231177:
My Prince!

The Gorgothian landing force has finally deigned to arrive on the battlefield.

Take note of their Catapults, as well as several strange-looking runners carrying explosive barrels.

These types of troops are quite capable of blowing up our walls, and without walls, My Prince, it will be a bit hard to hold the line.
Missions_en|669183009604231181: As My Prince amuses himself with his new pet, I’m filling in the ship’s log. Our aim is the acquisition of armor, banners and other Inverland artifacts. And although I suggested we steal all this on the quiet, Prince preferred a more direct approach. Namely, to destroy an entire enemy outpost.
Missions_en|669183009604231182:
My Prince certainly cannot be faulted for his tenacity and ingenuity. The failure of the peace talks (resulting in a horrific massacre) gave him the idea of how to ‘divide and conquer’ our enemies.

We'll create an illusion for our opponents that the fighting between them is more intense than it actually is. Which is why, today, we're attacking an Inverland outpost. Our goal is to capture their banners, armor, and other things of undoubted origin.

With the necessary equipment, we’ll be able to stage an attack by one enemy against another, which should eventually bring them to the negotiating table.
Missions_en|669183009612619789:
My Prince, apologies for keeping you stationed in that cramped office at the Headquarters, if that's what you can call a room under the stairs in the Rebel Barracks.

Still, it's all for the best, as the groom said to his run-away bride. If we were to build a Townhall right under the Inverlanders’ noses, the enemy would certainly have become suspicious…

Their suspicions in that case would have been absolutely justified: we are here to demolish the Inverland Outpost. In this regard, your ‘Headquarters’ could prove useful, as it is where you can recruit soldiers!
Missions_en|669183009612619790:
My Prince!

The Samreignian military doctrine, written by your great-grandfather, states the following: ‘The Inverlanders are no @#$%'n problem at all. They are suckers who can’t see @#$%. If you spot them, give'em a little tap with your sword, then drink some ale watching how they run away in panic.”

Either your great-grandfather underestimated the enemy’s capabilities, or the Inverlanders have learnt something over the past century. Because they not only noticed our presence, but even dared to launch an attack on the Headquarters.
Missions_en|1662889471313744442:
My Prince!

The House of the County Judge is destroyed!

There is no precise information on the consequences, but I prefer to believe that the Inverlanders are now deserting en masse. That looting has flourished, and the soldiers have fallen into complete moral decay.

If these assessments are correct, it is essential to intensify the offensive and crush the enemy. Demolish all remaining enemy Barracks and collect any stuff that might be useful for us to stage fake Inverland attacks on the Gorgoth Empire.
Missions_en|6213009872366781971:
My Prince!

Half of the enemy Barracks is destroyed!

There is no precise information on the consequences, but I prefer to believe that the Inverlanders are now deserting en masse. That looting has flourished, and the soldiers have fallen into complete moral decay.

If these assessments are correct, it’s time to crush the enemy immediately and demolish the remaining Barracks. After that, we can freely collect some useful stuff from the ruins to stage fake Inverland attacks on the Gorgoth Empire in the future.
Missions_en|5731528345704587159: Destroy the House of the County Judge
Missions_en|80484794124210321: Kill all the Inverlanders in the area
Missions_en|6522456948241061441: The Rebel Headquarters must not be destroyed
Missions_en|669183009608425472: My Prince’s unusual idea of staging an attack by Inverland on Gorgoth inevitably led to the need for a real attack. We need to destroy the Gorgothian fortress in order to then somehow convince the Emperor that Inverland was behind it.
Missions_en|669183009608425475:
My Prince grows very enthusiastic when he talks about the upcoming operation. Since he doesn’t talk to me about anything else, I’m starting to worry about his mental health.

We’re going to attack the Gorgothian Fortress and raise the Inverland flags over it. According to Connor’s plan, this will convince the Emperor that Inverland is on the offensive against historical Gorgothian lands.

Personally, I view the idea with some skepticism, since we have a Gorgothian spy in captivity who is ready to sabotage the Prince's plans whenever she gets the chance.
Missions_en|8504583909107975740:
My Prince!

You have so inspired the scouts that, when choosing a target for the staged Inverland attack on Gorgoth, they let their imaginations run wild.

We are not targeting some backwater village, a quarter of which is controlled by the Empire. Oh no, My Prince, we are storming one of the enemy’s most heavily guarded strongholds.

Our scouts are certain: by destroying the two main Gorgothian buildings, we will spread terror into the hearts of our enemies, break their will, thereby crowning our victory. May the Providence be with us, for it is too late to turn back now.
Missions_en|6840726683767950481:
I do not know who you are, crazy man, but you are doomed. Surrender immediately. I swear: neither you nor your men will come to any harm. On the contrary: we will send you to the finest healers in the Empire, so that they may cure the affliction that has clouded your mind.
